title: World
tagline: A listening map, never a single musical place.
summary: World music is a wide, imperfect umbrella often used for music outside dominant Western pop categories. It can include traditional, popular and experimental sounds from every region, each with its own history and audience. The label is useful for discovery but cannot describe the depth of any one tradition. These representative artists invite a wider journey, with attention to the places and communities from which their music grows.
origin_place: Global; no single place of origin

history.heading: Music belongs to place
history.text: Communities around the world developed music for ceremony, storytelling, dance and daily life. Instruments and musical systems carry histories that differ by region. No single timeline captures them all; each tradition deserves to be approached through its own context and practitioners.

history.heading: Records cross borders
history.text: Commercial recording and radio brought selected regional sounds to new listeners, often through the choices of collectors and labels. These pathways enabled discovery but could flatten context. Musicians continued to shape their own traditions, adapting to new audiences and technologies.

history.heading: A category becomes visible
history.text: The phrase world music gained wider use in the international record industry and festival programming. Collaborations connected musicians across continents, sometimes creating new forms and sometimes raising questions about representation. Listeners discovered more artists, while the category's breadth remained difficult to define.

history.heading: Direct exchange and discovery
history.text: Digital releases and global touring made it easier to encounter artists without relying on broad market labels. Musicians combine local traditions with contemporary production on their own terms. A thoughtful listening journey starts with curiosity and context rather than assuming that distant sounds are interchangeable.

pillars.name: Fela Kuti
pillars.why: Kuti's Afrobeat joined extended groove, ensemble interplay and political expression, becoming an influential Nigerian musical language.

pillars.name: Ravi Shankar
pillars.why: Shankar brought deep knowledge of Hindustani classical music to international stages while maintaining a distinct artistic tradition.

pillars.name: Miriam Makeba
pillars.why: Makeba carried South African song and performance to global audiences, connecting artistry with cultural history and advocacy.
